characteristics.name: Effect
characteristics.$text:
If this spell is cast with a casting result of 7 or more, the target friendly unit gains a +D3 modifier to one of the following characteristics (to a maximum of 10). If this
spell is cast with a casting result of 11 or more, the target friendly unit gains a +D3 modifier to two of the following characteristics (to a maximum of 10). This spell lasts until your next Start of Turn sub-phase.


- Movement
- Weapon Skill
- Initiative

characteristics.name: Effect
characteristics.$text:
Place a unit of 2D3 Zombies on the battlefield anywhere completely within 12" of this model, but not within 1" of any enemy models. This unit cannot declare a charge during the turn in which it was raised:


Note that units of Zombies that are created in this way are not worth any Victory Points, do not count as Core, and are considered to have a starting unit size of 10 models for the purposes of the Invocation of Nehek special rule.

characteristics.name: Effect
characteristics.$text: If this spell is cast with a casting result of 6 or more, a single friendly unit that has the Necromantic Undead special rule and is within the caster’s Command range gains the Reserve Move special rule. If this spell is cast with a casting result of 10 or more, every friendly unit that has the Necromantic Undead special rule and is within the caster’s Command range gains the Reserve Move special rule. This spell lasts until the end of this turn.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: During the Command sub-phase of their turn, this Vampire may attempt to resurrect fallen creatures of the night by making a Leadership test (using their own Leadership). If this test is passed, a single friendly unit of Fell Bats, Bat Swarms or Dire Wolves that is within 12" of this model recovers D6 lost Wounds.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: This Vampire gains the Terror special rule.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: This Vampiric Power may only be taken by a Vampire Lord that is a Level 3 Wizard. This Vampire increases their Level of Wizardry by 1.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: This Vampire gains the Invocation of Nehek special rule (as described on page 5).

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: Models whose troop type is ‘infantry’ only. This Vampire gains the Fly (10) rule, but cannot join a unit.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: Enemy units must make a Leadership test before making any rolls To Hit against this model during the Combat phase. If this test is failed, only rolls of a natural 6 will hit.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: This Vampire has a +1 modifier to its Wounds characteristic.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: Level 1 Wizard Vampires only. During the Combat phase, for each unsaved wound caused by this model's Attacks, it immediately makes one additional Attack. These additional Attacks cannot generate further Attacks.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
Any enemy model that wishes to issue a challenge whilst engaged in the same combat as a model with this Vampiric Power must first make a Leadership test (using their own Leadership.) Apply a +1 modifier to the dice roll for each point of difference between its Weapon Skill characteristic and that of the model with this Vampiric Power (to a maximum of +2).


If the test is passed, the challenge is issued as normal. If the test is failed, the challenge is not issued and the enemy model must Retire, following the rules for refusing a challenge. In addition, challenges issued by a model with this Vampiric Power cannot be refused.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: This Vampire gains the Strike First special rule.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: This Vampire gains the Hatred (all enemies) special rule.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
Your army must include at least one Wizard to be its Master of the Dead.If your army includes several Wizards, the Master of the Dead will be the one with the highest Level of Wizardry. If two or more models have the highest Wizard Level, you may choose which one is the Master of the Dead when writing your muster list. You must tell your opponent which model is your Master of the Dead before deploying your army.


Should your Master of the Dead be slain, the magical animus of the army starts to dissipate. As soon as your Master of the Dead is removed from play as a casualty, all friendly units with the Necromantic Undead special rule lose the Regeneration (X) special rule.


In addition, at the end of the phase in which your Master of the Dead was removed from play as a casualty, and during each of your Start of Turn sub-phases for the remainder of the game, all friendly units with the Necromantic Undead special rule that are currently on the battlefield must make a Leadership test. If this test is failed, the unit loses a number of Wounds equal to the amount by which it failed the test.


For example, your army’s Master of the Dead is destroyed during your opponent’s Shooting phase. At the end of that phase a unit of Skeleton Warriors (Ld 5) makes a Leadership test and rolls a 7 (failing the test by 2). That unit immediately loses two Wounds. During your next Start of Turn sub-phase, the same unit makes another Leadership test, this time rolling a 6, resulting in the loss of one Wound.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: Models with this special rule are not affected if the Master of the Dead for your army is slain. Furthermore, unless they have joined a unit that does not have this special rule they (and their mounts) can march as normal. In addition, A Vampire Count or Vampire Thrall Wizard with this special rule may wear armour or carry a shield without penalty. IE: They may Cast and Dispel as Normal.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: A hand weapon carried by a model with this special rule has the Magical Attacks special rule and an Armour Piercing characteristic of -1.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
If a model with this special rule rolls a natural 6 when making a roll To Wound for an attack made in combat, it has struck
a ‘Cleaving Blow.’ Enemy models whose troop type is ‘regular infantry,’ ‘heavy infantry,’ ‘light cavalry,’ ‘heavy cavalry’ or ‘war beasts’ are not permitted an armour or Regeneration save against a Cleaving Blow (Ward saves can be attempted as normal).


Note that if an attack wounds automatically, this special rule cannot be used.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
A unit with this special rule that is arrayed in a Close Order formation, and that is equipped with and chooses to use shields, may choose not to Give Ground should it lose a round of combat.


However, if the winning side significantly outnumbers the losing side, it will overwhelm the loser. If the Unit Strength of the winning side is more than twice that of the losing side, this unit cannot use this special rule and must Give Ground as normal.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
A unit with this special rule reduces the number of wounds suffered due to the Unstable special rule by the number shown in brackets (shown here as ‘X’).


Note that this special rule is not cumulative. If two or more models in a unit have this special rule, use the highest value for the entire unit. For example, if a character with Indomitable (2) joins a unit with Indomitable (1), the whole unit uses the character’s Indomitable (2) special rule.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
Models with this special rule are ‘Undead’. Undead models cannot march (unless they have the Fly (X) special rule and choose to move by flying). In addition, all Undead models have the following universal special rules:

- Fear
- Immune to Psychology
- Unbreakable
- Unstable 


A character with this special rule cannot join a unit without this special rule, and vice versa.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
During the Command sub-phase of their turn, if they are not engaged in combat, this character may attempt to resurrect the fallen (see page 28) by making a Leadership test (using their own Leadership). If this test is passed, a single friendly unit that has the Necromantic Undead special rule and is within 12" of this character recovers a number of lost Wounds. However, magically repairing great Undead beasts is much harder than
raising Zombies from the dirt. Therefore, how many Wounds are recovered depends upon the unit’s troop type and this character’s Level of Wizardry:


- If the unit’s troop type is ‘regular infantry’ or ‘swarms,’ it recovers a number of Wounds equal to this character’s Level of Wizardry +D3.
- If the unit’s troop type is ‘light cavalry’ or ‘war beasts,’ it recovers a number of Wounds equal to this character’s Level of Wizardry +1.
- If the unit’s troop type is ‘heavy infantry,’ ‘monstrous infantry,’ ‘heavy cavalry,’ ‘monstrous cavalry’ or ‘light chariot,’ it recovers a number of Wounds equal to this character’s Level of Wizardry.
- If the unit’s troop type is ‘heavy chariot,’ ‘monstrous creature,’ ‘behemoth’ or ‘war machine,’ it recovers a single Wound.
- Models with the Dark Vitality or Ethereal special rules recover half the amount of wounds as described above (including any bonuses), rounding fractions up.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: When resurrecting the fallen, a unit with this special rule can be taken beyond its starting size by an additional 20 models.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
In a Vampire Counts army, it is possible to heal a unit by recovering lost Wounds, and to resurrect fallen warriors. Wounds recovered in this way follow a strict order:

•	First, any characters that have joined the unit are healed. A character that has been reduced to zero Wounds and removed from play cannot be resurrected.

•	Second, models with more than one Wound on their profile are healed.

•	Next, the unit champion is resurrected, displacing rank-and-file models as required, followed by the standard bearer and musician.

•	Finally, rank-and-file models are resurrected.

Note that, in the case of multiple Wound models, each model must be fully healed, recovering all of its lost Wounds, before another can be healed or resurrected.

Note also that at least one model must remain in order for a unit to be healed. In other words, a unit that has been reduced to zero Wounds and removed from play cannot be resurrected.

Resurrected models are added to the front rank until it reaches the minimum required to claim a Rank Bonus, after which additional models can be added to the front or rear rank. If the unit already has more than one rank, models can only be added to the rear rank. A unit cannot be taken beyond its starting size.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: A unit comprised entirely of modes with this special rule treats all terrain as open ground for the purposes of movement. They cannot end their movement inside impassable terrain, though they can pass through it.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
At the end of a Combat phase in which a unit with this special rule caused one or more unsaved wounds, roll a D6 for each unsaved wound caused. For each roll of 5+, models with this special rule recover one lost Wound, following the rules for Resurrecting the Fallen. However, a model with the Behemoth troop type may only ever recover a maximum of one Wound per phase in this manner.


In addition, if a unit with this special rule wishes to Pursue or Overrun, it must make a Leadership test. If this test is failed, the unit still Pursues or Overruns, but rolls a single D6 to determine the distance moved, rather than the usual 2D6.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
A model with this special rule may make a ‘Wailing Dirge’ attack. A Wailing Dirge attack is a Shooting attack with the Magical Attacks special rule and a range of 8”. A Wailing Dirge attack can target an enemy Lone character regardless of the usual rules for targeting Lone characters. If this model is engaged in combat during the Shooting phase, it may target a unit in base contact with a Wailing Dirge attack and may do so even if it charged this turn.


A Wailing Dirge attack does not roll to hit and wound as normal. Instead, the target must make a Leadership test with a negative modifier to its Leadership characteristic shown in the brackets after the name of this special rule (shown here as ‘X’). If this test is failed, the target suffers a number of wounds equal to the amount by which it failed the test, with no armour or Regeneration saves permitted (Ward saves can be attempted as normal).


Note that a Wailing Dirge attack may reduce the target's Leadership characteristic to a minimum of 2

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
A Wizard with the ‘Lore of Undeath’ special rule may discard one of their randomly generated spells as normal. When they do so, they may select instead either the signature spell of their chosen Lore of Magic, or one of the spells listed below:

• Vanhal’s Danse Macabre - Renegades
• Hellish Vigour - Renegades
• Raise Dead - Renegades

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: Enemy units engaged in combat with this model suffer a -1 modifier to their Weapon Skill characteristic.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: In combat, this model may make one of its attacks each turn with this weapon

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: Even if engaged in combat, this model can cast Scrying Pool, with a Power Level of 2

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: Enemy units must make a Leadership test before making any rolls To Hit against this model during the Combat phase. If this test is failed, only rolls of a natural 6 will hit.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: Whilst within this model’s Command range, friendly units with the Necromantic Undead special rule gain a +1 modifier to their Movement and Initiative characteristics.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: All Wizards (friend or foe) may apply a +1 modifier to any Casting roll whilst within the Command range of one or more models with this special rule. However, if any Wizard miscasts whilst within this model’s Command range, they must roll twice on the Miscast table and apply both results.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: In combat, this model must make one of its attacks each turn with this weapon.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: When this model loses its last Wound and is removed from play, every unit in base contact with it (friend or foe) suffers D6 Strength 2 hits, each with an AP of -1.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
A Vampire Thrall that has been upgraded to be your Battle Standard Bearer replaces the "Hold Your Ground" rule given in the Warhammer: the Old World rulebook with the version given below:
**"Hold Your Ground":** Friendly units within the Battle Standard Bearer’s Command range may re-roll any failed Leadership test. In addition, friendly units within the Battle Standard Bearer’s Command range reduce the number of Wounds lost due to the Unstable special rule by D3.

*Note that this is not cumulative with the Indomitable (X) special rule. If a unit is affected by both, use the highest value.*

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
When a friendly unit that is within 12" of this model recovers a number of lost Wounds due to a character using the Invocation of Nehek special rule, roll a D6. On a roll of 4+ add +1 to the result. In addition, friendly units within 12" of one or more models with this special rule reduce the number of Wounds lost due to the Unstable special rule by 1.

*Note that this is cumulative with the Indomitable (X) special rule.*

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: Enemy Wizards that are within 18" of one or more models with this special rule when attempting to cast a spell must increase that spell’s casting value by 1.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: Whilst within 6" of one or more models with this special rule, friendly units of Zombies lose the Shambling Hordes special rule, gain the Newly Dead special rule, and modify their Weapon Skill characteristic by +1. In addition, whenever a friendly unit of Zombies within 6" of one or more models with this special rule recovers lost Wounds due to the Invocation of Nehek special rule, it recovers an additional D3 Wounds.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: If a model with this special rule is your General, all Crypt Ghouls, Crypt Horrors and Vargulfs gain the Vanguard special rule.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: No armour save is permitted against wounds caused by this weapon (Ward and Regeneration saves can be attempted as normal).

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
A Wight Lord that has been upgraded to be your Battle Standard Bearer replaces the "Hold Your Ground" rule given in the Warhammer: the Old World rulebook with the version given below:
**"Hold Your Ground":** Friendly units within the Battle Standard Bearer's Command range may re-roll any failed Leadership test. In addition, friendly units within the Battle Standard Bearer’s Command range reduce the number of Wounds lost due to the Unstable special rule by D3.
*Note that this is not cumulative with the Indomitable (X) special rule. If a unit is affected by both, use the highest value.*

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: A unit with this special rule never receives an initiative bonus for charging an enemy in its front, flank or rear arc. In addition, when this unit Pursues or Overruns, roll a single D6 to determine the distance moved, rather than the usual 2D6.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: At the start of the Combat phase, any enemy unit in base contact with one or more models with this special rule must make a Leadership test. If this test is failed, that unit gains the Strikes Last special rule until the end of the phase.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: To maintain Skirmish formation, every model in this unit must be within 3" of another model belonging to the same unit, rather than the usual 1". However, unlike most Skirmishers, models with this special rule do not have a 360° vision arc; they instead have a 90° vision arc, corresponding to their front arc.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: Unlike other swarms, this unit is not subject to the Undisciplined rule. In other words, this unit can use the Inspiring Presence rule of the army’s General and the Hold your Ground rule of a Battle Standard.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: Every model in a unit of Blood Knights can issue and accept challenges in the same manner as a character. However, a unit with this special rule cannot refuse a challenge – if a challenge is issued and a model belonging to this unit could accept it, a model belonging to the unit must accept it.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: During a turn in which it charged, this model has a +1 modifier to its Strength characteristic.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: A unit with this special rule may perform a ‘Spectral Reapers’ attack against a single enemy unit that is not engaged in combat. To do so, this unit must move (by flying) over the unit it wishes to attack during the Remaining Moves sub-phase. Once this unit’s movement is complete, the enemy unit suffers a single Strength 4 hit, with no armour save permitted (Ward and Regeneration saves can be attempted as normal), and with the Flaming Attacks and Magical Attacks special rules, for each model in this unit that moved over it.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: A Spectral lance can only be used during a turn in which the wielder charged, and its Strength and Armour Piercing modifiers apply only against enemy models the wielder charged that turn.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
A Black Coach is not wholly corporeal. To represent this, a Black Coach may become ‘Incorporeal’ during the Command sub-phase of its turn, and will remain Incorporeal until your next Start of Turn sub-phase. Whilst Incorporeal, a Black Coach:
- Loses the Impact Hits (D6+2) special rule.
- Gains the Ethereal and Fly (10) special rules.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: No armour save is permitted against wounds caused by this weapon (Ward and Regeneration saves can be attempted as normal).

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: Enemy units cannot claim any bonus combat result points for being engaged with this model’s flank or rear arc.
